note: Thursday 8 Oct 2026 run, 07:02 SGT, before Asia's open. Latest completed US cash session is Wednesday 7 Oct close (S&P 500 7,801.77 -0.22%, Nasdaq 27,538.69 -0.22%, VIX 15.08 +0.47%) -- a pullback from Tuesday's record close as FOMC minutes confirmed the Fed's hawkish Sept hike and the 10-year yield hit a 24-year high. CNN Fear&Greed's own page again blocked automated fetch (HTTP 451/418); mirrors (benzinga, finhacker, macromicro) converge on the index holding in Neutral territory (~47), carried at the same reading as Tuesday's confirmed level pending a cleaner pull. Crypto Fear&Greed eased to 71 (Greed) from 73 as Bitcoin fell 2.78%. Breadth internals (% above 200/50-DMA, McClellan, sector breadth) are still dated Oct 6 -- the freshest independently-confirmed reading available; narrow breadth (only 3 of 11 sectors healthily above 200-DMA) persists even as the index sits near record highs. Flows remain the week-ended-~Oct-1 BofA/EPFR edition (next due ~Oct 8-10) -- the biggest US equity outflow since March ($21.1B) and the biggest China inflow in 9 weeks ($3.7B) as mainland markets reopened post Golden Week.

flows.period: week ending ~Oct 1, 2026 (BofA Flow Show / EPFR Global, lagged weekly data released Oct 2-3)
flows.narrative: The latest available weekly flow data shows a rotation away from US equities into cash, bonds and hard-asset hedges, even as China and broader EM equity funds extended a multi-week inflow streak on the Golden Week reopen. Gold drew steady inflows as a diversifying hedge even as its spot price corrected, while credit markets shifted from corporate high-grade/high-yield into longer-duration government paper.
